title: Consecutive Preferential Bayesian Optimization
abstract: arXiv:2511.05163v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Preferential Bayesian optimization allows optimization of objectives that are either expensive or difficult to measure directly, by relying on a minimal number of comparative evaluations done by a human expert. Generating candidate solutions for evaluation is also often expensive, but existing preferential optimization methods do not account for this production cost. We introduce Consecutive Preferential Bayesian Optimization (CPBO) for the consecutive setting, where production cost is reduced by reusing the previous candidate in each comparison. We also account for the perceptual ambiguity of the oracle providing the feedback by incorporating a Just-Noticeable Difference threshold into a probabilistic preference model to capture indifference to small utility differences. translated_abstract: 偏好贝叶斯优化通过依赖人类专家进行的最少数量的比较评估，能够对那些成本高昂或难以直接测量的目标进行优化。然而，生成用于评估的候选方案本身也往往代价高昂，而现有的偏好优化方法并未考虑这种生产成本。我们提出了面向连续（consecutive）设定的连续偏好贝叶斯优化（CPBO），通过在每次比较中复用上一个候选方案来降低生产成本。我们还考虑了提供反馈的评估者的感知模糊性，通过在概率偏好模型中引入最小可觉差阈值，来刻画其对微小效用差异表现出的无差别态度。我们将一种基于信息论的采集策略适配到该设定中，在预设的约束下选择对未知最优解信息量最大的新配置。
tldr: 该论文提出连续偏好贝叶斯优化（CPBO），通过在每次比较中复用上一个候选方案来降低候选方案的生产成本，并在概率偏好模型中引入最小可觉差（JND）阈值以处理评估者的感知模糊性，同时适配信息论采集策略来高效逼近未知最优解。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes Consecutive Preferential Bayesian Optimization (CPBO), which reduces candidate production cost by reusing the previous candidate in each comparison, incorporates a Just-Noticeable Difference threshold into a probabilistic preference model to account for the oracle's perceptual ambiguity, and adapts an information-theoretic acquisition strategy to efficiently approach the unknown optimum.
